recipes.name: Cheesy Green Bean Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 (10.75 ounce) cans condensed cream of mushroom soup
2 (16 ounce) packages frozen French cut green beans
0.5 pound processed cheese food (eg. Velveeta), sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish with cooking spray.
Mix together condensed soup, Cheddar cheese, milk, and 1/2 of the onions in a large bowl until well combined.

Layer the bottom of the prepared dish with 1/2 of the green beans. Pour 1/2 of the soup mixture over beans and sprinkle with 1/2 of the processed cheese. Repeat layering one more time, then top with remaining onions.
Bake casserole in the preheated oven until hot and bubbly, 30 to 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Green Bean Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This cheesy green bean casserole is made with frozen green beans and features 2 kinds of grated cheese for a tasty Thanksgiving side.

review.reviewBody: Although we all enjoyed this casserole, I felt like the Velveeta was unneccesary. It would still be cheesy without it, and the Velveeta did not melt properly, causing there to be "globs" of it all through the casserole. I will make this again, just will leave the Velveeta out.

My husband normally hates green bean casseroles, however, I knew the cheese would win him over! I halved the recipe, using (1) 27 oz. can of green beans, and only (1) 10.75 oz. can of cream of mushroom soup. The cheese is the key-Did not add any Velveeta, used grated Colby 1/2 to 3/4C, more on top along with a sprinkle of parmesan cheese. Definitely for the cheese lovers! Will make again using French green beans.

I used this recipe and mixed it with another recipe and it worked really well. I omitted the Velveeta altogether. The cheddar was enough.

I also added 1 lb portabella mushrooms sautéed with shallots in some butter to the mushroom soup mixture. I layered the beans and sauce like the recipe said. It came out really good! So, it was more like a cheesy mushroom/green bean casserole!

I made this and it was delicious, but I made a couple simple changes:

If you use canned green beans (I used string beans) then use 4+ cans.

I added cheese to sight/instinct, I did not add 1/2 pound- maybe 1/3 tops.

I also added more flavor to the mushroom soup mix by using pepper, minced garlic, onion powder and salt. I feel like that made a big difference, because the flavor was wonderful! 

I will definitely make this again!

I have always used this recipe for my green bean casserole. The changes I make, is to use canned green beans, not frozen. I don't like the crunchiness. Also, instead of Velveeta, I use slices of cheddar and munster cheese. It is always a huge hit at parties.

this dish is always requested by my husband's family. I have made it with canned, frozen, and fresh green beans, and is 100 times better with fresh green beans. I also took the advice of another cook, and didn't even bother layering, add french fried onions to the top during the last 15 min of cooking, so you can stir just before adding them.

I loved this green bean recipe! I made it for Thanksgiving and everybody loved them. I will be making this for Christmas too! I left out the processed cheese and just used shredded cheddar cheese. It was the perfect amount of cheese and cheesey taste. I couldn't imagine how this dish would taste with all the extra velveeta added...

This is Wonderful!!!! I used 2 cans of green beans instead of the frozen so the dish isn't so crunchy, and baked for about 45-60 minutes. Even if you don't like green bean casserole, you must try this. It is sooooooo good!! thank you Chris

This recipe is a good start, but it needs a lot of adjustments. I made it for Thanksgiving. Half my guests thought it had too much cheese; and the other half thought it needed more green beans. It also makes a huge amount. I halved the recipe and it was easily enough for 8 to 10 people. If I make it again, I will half everything else, but use 21 oz (roughly a bag and a half) of green beans to balance it. I have read others who recommend loosing the Velveeta altogether. You could do that and still have a fine casserole, but the cheddar alone wouldn't generate the super cheesy flavor that makes this recipe a keeper in my recipe box.

Made this for Thanksgiving tonight and it is the bomb! Everyone loved it and said this will be the new green bean casserole! I did not add the velveeta and added Worcestershire sauce and it was a hit!

I took this to Thanksgiving today; forget the kids, the adults loved it. Everyone got seconds. The recipe seemed a little runny at first but if the dish has to sit a while it turned out just right. I layered the recipe just as it indicates but ended up stirring it after 30 minutes of cooking. The Velveeta melts but in patches. Don't bother layer it. Just mix it all together and add the fried onions during the last 10 minutes of baking. I used canned french green beans and only used one cup of cheedar. Super easy and fast. I will use this recipe again.
rated 'the best green bean casserole I ever made' by friends and family
This is one of our family favorites. Our daughter request that I make it for every Thanks Giving and Christmas Dinners.
Me and my girlfriend loved this! I did not use the velveeta I just used shredded cheese and salt and pepper and it was perfect!
Made this for Christmas dinner on it was a big hit! I omitted the Velveeta and mixed all ingredients together except for a onions for the top. Also added a bit of soy sauce. Will make again! So easy.

Amazing! Second year making this for a side dish on thanksgiving and it's a hit every time! Everyone says it's the best green bean casserole they've ever had. I don't think it's too cheesy as some people commented. It's perfect if you follow the ingredients!
use half as much soup & cheese. added bacon and mushrooms
Used 1 cup of chedder cheese instead of velveeta and it was delicious. Will make this again.

Very disappointed......WAY to cheesy. It should be called cheese casserole with a few green beans. Next time I would omit the velvetta, cut the cheddar cheese in half and maybe add a little bit of salt.
Holy cheese! I love cheesy green bean casserole but I'm making some changes next time. The velveeta was too much for me and I'd use canned green beans instead.
